requirement.evidence: Provided that a dwelling is registered in accordance with § 155-30 upon the vacation of a residential apartment unit by a tenant, the apartment unit shall become decontrolled and exempt from the provisions of this chapter for the new tenant's initial rental; provided, however, that said rental shall be limited to an increase of 25% over the last rental paid by the tenant who voluntarily vacated the rental unit
requirement.note: Once per three years is in § 155-34: "No dwelling unit shall be decontrolled pursuant to this article more than once in any three-year period." Later increases are controlled per § 155-31.

key_value.evidence: said rental shall be limited to an increase of 25% over the last rental paid by the tenant who voluntarily vacated the rental unit, exclusive of any capital improvement surcharge that is a component of said last rental.
key_value.note: The once-per-3-year limit is in § 155-34. The 25% is exclusive of capital improvement surcharge.

status.evidence: Provided that a dwelling is registered in accordance with § 155-30 upon the vacation of a residential apartment unit by a tenant, the apartment unit shall become decontrolled and exempt from the provisions of this chapter for the new tenant's initial rental
status.note: Presented as current code; the document is a 2024 third-party copy, so a reviewer should confirm against the official code.

citation.note: §§ 155-32 and 155-34 are also in the document.

requirement.evidence: At the expiration of a lease or at the termination of a lease of a periodic tenant, no landlord may request or receive a percentage increase in rent which is greater than 5% or the percentage difference between the consumer price index three months prior to the expiration or termination of the lease and three months prior to the commencement of the lease term, whichever is less.
requirement.note: Most is supported: the 5%/CPI cap, once per 12 months, 30 days' notice with reasons (§ 155-4), the substantial compliance certificate (§ 155-26), void excess increases and refunds, and the two-year limit. The card's "once in any 12 months" and "only when your lease ends" are slight simplifications, since periodic tenants and leases under one year are treated differently.

key_value.evidence: No more than one such cost-of-living rental increase in any one twelve-month period shall be permitted irrespective of the number of different tenants occupying said housing space during said twelve-month period.
key_value.note: The lesser of 5% or CPI is in § 155-5.

status.note: Presented as current code, amended 2-1-2023. The document is a 2024 third-party copy.
